page.layout: One page of text inside a decorative woodcut border; running head at top with page number at right; no margin notes on the printed page (left edge shows a neighbouring page, not counted). Text runs in one block from top to bottom, with a line of centred text and a catchword-like fragment "D de" at the foot.

p.i: endi seipsum, quidquid moliatur artifex. Ipsum destruere, ac in esse reducere, fatuum esset opus, cum ex eo nihil plus virtutis, neq; potentia haberi possit, quam obtinet ex propria sua natura. Nulla sit reductio eorum, quae natura perficit in speciem, vel in individuum, nisi primò corrumpantur. Etiam post corruptionem generatio non fit speciei similis, nisi fiat regressus in hoc genus. Quapropter auri destructio viam non sternit ad ipsum construendum, quia per sui destructionem construi nihil potest; Ipso namq; mortuo pariter moritur ejus substantia, ut ex eo non possit amplius aliud argentum vivum enasci, neq; metallum, & cætera, quæ ibidem sequuntur, notatu condigna.

main_text.p: Ut igitur sententiam nostram D de

page.notes: The first line of the page is a fragment continuing the previous paragraph ("endi seipsum"); the text is italic throughout. The printed line "Ut igitur sententiam nostram" is centred and followed by a line with a large initial "D" and "de", which may be a signature or catchword and is uncertain. Ligatures and long s rendered as plain s. The left edge shows a neighbouring page's text and is excluded.
